candidates.text: ​Diaries: Fishing Lessons For the short film Fishing Lessons , New York-based filmmaker Guy Kozak reflects on romantic relationships through angling and the traditions of male bonding, creating an intimate memento to mark his first wedding anniversary. Shooting over one day in Cape Cod – where his wife grew up and where they were married the previous year – Kozak cast his stepfather-in-law Nat, and his closest friends, Bo & Bill, to deliver their advice on love, life, and fishing, captured against the stillness of the coastal landscape. - Guy Kozak Working with five rolls of expired 16mm film, Kozak embraces the unpredictability and warping of an imperfect medium, while mirroring the uncertainties of both fishing and human connection. Drawing inspiration from the poetic documentary-style of U.S. filmmaker Les Blank, Kozak frames the fishing tradition as a shared space for peace and reflection, highlighting the intimacy, sentimentality and gentleness often missing from portrayals of masculinity.
